statement_verbatim:
statement: >-
  Every concrete tracking-plan item's logical artifact is produced by exactly one product capability's
  produce[] telemetry declaration, and the item's owner names that product capability (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Metric tracking-plan items declare only low- or medium-cardinality dimensions, and no dimension
  names a property declared cardinality high (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every JSON file under the telemetry root is one concrete tracking-plan item at
  `telemetry/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>].json`, shape-valid
  against telemetry-plan.schema.json, with its id and logical artifact mirroring its path, a SemVer
  version, and no concrete id declared twice (REQUIRED).

statement: A theme is a repository-defined kebab-case namespace for plan artifacts. The only
  reserved entry is index 0, which MUST be commons; repositories declare every other theme
  in plan/_themes.yaml. Theme membership and identity-prefix consistency are enforceable.

statement: Every product capability, user/system flow, flow router, and contract theme MUST resolve to a value in the
  repository-owned plan/_themes.yaml registry. The package provides no default taxonomy.

statement: 'plan/_themes.yaml MUST declare commons at theme index 0. Repositories may add any
  valid theme at other indexes, but may not replace or remove the commons floor.'

statement: A themed product capability's produced artifact, contract, and telemetry identity prefix MUST equal
  the product capability theme.

statement: Every platform:acceptance:commit-failure.cause (version_conflict, authorization_refused, idempotency_conflict, authority_unavailable) MUST be reachable, registered in the dispatch graph, resolvable, and terminating - or an explicit tracked-and-expiring deferral. Pending binding - validator owned by D5 (#1089).

statement: A user/system flow may carry an optional acceptances block (DESIRED OUTCOME acceptance shape);
  each contributes a derived repo rule via the rule-binding walker.

statement: Artifacts flow between participants as {domain}:{resource}; they must be produced before consumed
  and be defined in participant product capability manifests.

statement: "The category FIELD classifies a user/system flow as nominal, error, alternate, or exception. It is
  metadata on the user/system flow, never encoded in its identity, so reclassifying a user/system flow
  changes a field and not its name."

statement: A user/system flow is an executable end-to-end system/user journey — a strictly-linear,
  ordered sequence of steps that moves artifacts across a set of product capabilities from a declared
  initial input to exactly one terminal contract, telling ONE coherent journey. This
  is a planner domain-decomposition artifact naming WHAT journey the domain must support;
  how the journey is run and whether it holds state at runtime are coder/tester concerns.
  This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly; the enforceable
  parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes that require it.

statement: A user/system flow references prerequisite user/system flows as user-system-flow:{user_system_flow_id}; foundation (commons) user/system flows often
  precede others; data-flow consumers depend on producers; circular dependencies are forbidden.

statement: 'A composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> user_system_flow_id dispatch key is exceptional:
  permitted only with a behavioral_difference justification, discriminant exactly
  one field:value.'

statement: The divergence dispatch map is a declared, schema-valid registry (artifact_urn
  -> user_system_flow_id) that the journey router reads; routing is never an imperative in-code
  map.

statement: The declared family MUST agree with the declared terminal contract - family:delivery iff the terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit AND the terminal primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; family:behavior otherwise; a missing family field is invalid. Pending binding - validator owned by D1 (#1085).

statement: The family classifies a user/system flow as behavior or delivery, orthogonal to the variant category (0-3). The declared terminal contract is the source of truth; the family field is the validator-checked assertion and is never encoded in the user/system flow ID.

statement: Every DESIRED OUTCOME obligation surfaces as message, self-message, guard, fragment,
  invariant, or explicit structural residual.
